record.original_question: For the princess and monster game on a tree, does there exist an optimal princess strategy with the confluency property that whenever two princess trajectories meet at some time t0, they coincide for all earlier times up to t0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the princess-and-monster search game played on a finite tree $T$ (a connected graph without cycles, viewed as a metric space with unit-length edges). Two players, the princess (hider) and the monster (searcher), move continuously along $T$ with speeds bounded by $1$. Neither player can see the other; capture occurs at the first time $t \ge 0$ at which the two players occupy the same point of $T$. The princess wishes to maximize, and the monster wishes to minimize, the expected capture time.

A (mixed) strategy for the princess is a probability distribution over Lipschitz trajectories $p:[0,\infty) \to T$ with $|p'| \le 1$ almost everywhere. Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the support of such a strategy. The strategy is said to have the confluency property if for every pair of trajectories $p_1, p_2 \in \mathcal{P}$ and every time $t_0 \ge 0$ such that $p_1(t_0) = p_2(t_0)$, one has $p_1(t) = p_2(t)$ for all $t \in [0, t_0]$ (i.e., trajectories that meet at some time must have coincided at every earlier time).

Question: For the princess-and-monster game on an arbitrary finite tree, does there exist an optimal strategy for the princess that satisfies the confluency property?
artifact.status_search_result: The princess-and-monster game on general networks (beyond the circle) remains largely unsolved, and no published resolution of the tree confluency conjecture was found. Searches return general background on the game with no result establishing existence of an optimal confluent princess strategy on trees.

status_evidence.title: Princess and monster game - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Only the circle network has been solved; the game on most other networks remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The princess-and-monster game on most networks, including trees, is unsolved, indicating related conjectures remain open.

status_evidence.title: The 'Princess and Monster' Game on an Interval
status_evidence.snippet: The full solution of this very simple game is still open and appears difficult.
status_evidence.claim: Even on an interval the game is open, so finer structural conjectures about optimal strategies on trees are not resolved.
